description: Implement the real research logic behind the FEAT-001 abstractions: the concrete source connectors (public-domain Bible text, original-language Strong's/lexicon, historical/commentary/Church-Fathers), the LLM synthesis that produces the 'common misconception vs. deeper truth' dossier with mandatory citations, the versioned dossier JSON Schema, and the JSON + Markdown output writers. Live mode uses the network/LLM keys; dry-run uses bundled fixtures + stub provider and must still produce a complete, schema-valid sample dossier.
steps: Finalize deepresearch/schema/dossier.schema.json: a versioned JSON Schema (include a schema_version field, matching deepresearch.SCHEMA_VERSION) describing the dossier contract for downstream bots. Required top-level fields: schema_version; query (raw input) and resolved_reference(s); misconception (surface/common reading) and deeper_truth (better-supported meaning) as REQUIRED sections; translations (array of {translation, reference, text, citation}); original_language_terms (array of {term, transliteration, strongs, language ('Greek'|'Hebrew'), definition, insight, citation}); historical_context (array of {text, citation}); commentary (array of {author/source, excerpt, citation}); cross_references (array of {reference, note, citation}); talking_points (array sized for an ~8-20 min long-form script); gaps (array recording any unavailable sources); and a citations index. Define a Citation shape (source name + locator/URL) and require that every substantive claim object carries a citation.
Update deepresearch/models.py dataclasses to match the finalized schema and add to_json()/to_dict() helpers and a validate() that checks against dossier.schema.json via jsonschema.

Implement deepresearch/sources/bible_api.py: connector for bible-api.com (confirmed reachable this session: GET https://bible-api.com/<ref>?translation=<kjv|web|asv>). Fetch the target verse AND the surrounding passage per config.context_window, across config.translations (public-domain only). Build Citation with the source name + request URL. Route all HTTP through cache.py so dry-run/tests replay fixtures. NEVER request copyrighted modern translations (NIV/ESV) — restrict to the public-domain allowlist and reject others.

Implement deepresearch/sources/strongs.py: original-language key-term extraction using public-domain Strong's lexicon data. Bundle a small public-domain Strong's dataset (or a fixtures subset) so the common terms in the sample verses resolve offline; map pivotal words to Strong's numbers + Greek/Hebrew lemma + public-domain definition, and attach citations. Design so a fuller dataset can be dropped in later without code changes.

Implement deepresearch/sources/commentary.py: connector(s) for public-domain historical/cultural context and classic commentary / Church-Father excerpts from CCEL (ccel.org), New Advent Fathers (newadvent.org), sacred-texts.com, and Project Gutenberg. Respect robots.txt/ToS (document the allowlist + a user-agent; skip disallowed paths and record a gap) and cache everything fetched. For dry-run, serve bundled public-domain excerpts from fixtures.

Register all connectors in the registry and wire pipeline.py stages to call them for real, with graceful degradation: if a connector fails or is offline without a fixture, append a structured entry to dossier.gaps and continue (never crash the run).

Implement deepresearch/llm/prompts.py: a synthesis system+user prompt template that (a) is handed ALL gathered source material (translations, original-language terms, historical/commentary excerpts) with their citations, (b) instructs the model to produce the misconception->deeper-truth structure, (c) REQUIRES every substantive claim to cite one of the provided sources by name+locator and to add nothing unsourced, (d) instructs it to FLAG uncertainty instead of inventing, and (e) enforces NON-DENOMINATIONAL neutrality (66-book shared-canon baseline; note tradition differences neutrally; center the person and teaching of Jesus Christ). Keep prompts provider-agnostic.

Implement deepresearch/synthesis.py: assembles the gathered materials, calls the selected LLMProvider with the prompt, parses the result into the dossier model, and runs a post-synthesis integrity check that drops/flags any claim lacking a resolvable citation and records uncertainty. The stub provider returns deterministic, fixture-grounded content so dry-run yields a complete, schema-valid dossier.

Implement the output writers in pipeline.write_output: write <output_dir>/<slug>.json (schema-valid) and a human-readable <output_dir>/<slug>.md with clearly labeled sections (Misconception, Deeper Truth, Original-Language Insight, Historical Context, Commentary, Cross-References, Talking Points, Sources, Gaps). The flow is human-review-gated: no auto-publishing.
Ensure `--dry-run` end-to-end for both a verse ('Matthew 5:17') and a topic ('turn the other cheek') produces a complete dossier that validates against the schema.
acceptance_criteria: Dry-run for a verse and for a topic each produce a JSON dossier that validates against deepresearch/schema/dossier.schema.json (schema_version matches SCHEMA_VERSION) and a readable Markdown dossier.
The dossier always contains populated 'misconception' and 'deeper_truth' sections and a non-empty talking_points list sized for long-form.
Every substantive claim object in the dossier carries a Citation (source name + locator/URL); the integrity check removes or flags any uncited claim.
Requesting a copyrighted modern translation (e.g. NIV) is rejected / not fetched; only public-domain translations are retrieved.
An unavailable source is recorded in dossier.gaps and does not crash the run (graceful degradation).
verification: Run: unset OPENAI_API_KEY ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; .venv/bin/python -m deepresearch research "Matthew 5:17" --dry-run then validate the emitted JSON against the schema with jsonschema (e.g. a one-off python snippet) and confirm it passes.
Run the same for the topic: .venv/bin/python -m deepresearch research "turn the other cheek" --dry-run and confirm a schema-valid dossier with populated misconception/deeper_truth.
Inspect the produced Markdown and confirm the labeled sections and a Sources section listing citations are present.
findings: Implemented the real research logic on top of FEAT-001. Finalized dossier.schema.json as a draft-07 versioned schema (schema_version == SCHEMA_VERSION 0.1.0) with required misconception/deeper_truth claim objects (each requires >=1 citation), translations/original_language_terms/historical_context/commentary/cross_references/talking_points (minItems 1)/gaps and a flat citations index; additionalProperties:false throughout. Rewrote models.py to match with to_dict/to_json/validate and build_citation_index. Added real connectors: bible_api.py (bible-api.com, public-domain allowlist kjv/web/asv/bbe/ylt/dra/oeb-us, hard-refuses NIV/ESV before building any URL, expands target verse to a passage via context_window, routes HTTP through cache.py and falls back to fixtures offline), strongs.py (data-driven public-domain Strong's subset, drop-in larger dataset without code change), commentary.py (CCEL/New Advent/sacred-texts/Gutenberg host allowlist + user-agent + disallowed-path skipping, cached, fixtures in dry-run). pipeline._default_registry registers all three; stages map results to the new model with graceful degradation (gaps appended, never crashes). synthesis.py assembles a citation-carrying brief, calls the provider, parses the misconception->deeper_truth spine + talking_points + cross_references, and runs an integrity check that drops talking points lacking a resolvable citation and attaches/flags fallback citations for required claims (honest 'deepresearch integrity check' provenance when zero sources exist, so a fully-unsourced run still validates and does not crash). Rewrote stub_provider.py to be fixture-grounded, reusing only citations present in the brief and emitting 8+ talking points. Expanded prompts.py (citation/uncertainty/neutrality rules, JSON contract, build_user_prompt). write_output validates against the schema and writes <slug>.json + a labeled <slug>.md (Misconception, Deeper Truth, Original-Language Insight, Historical Context, Commentary, Cross-References, Talking Points, Sources, Gaps) with a DRAFT/human-review banner. Added 'turn the other cheek' topic fixtures and cross-reference fixtures. VERIFIED: dry-run for 'Matthew 5:17' and 'turn the other cheek' both produce schema-valid dossiers (schema_version matches, populated misconception/deeper_truth, 8-9 talking points); NIV rejected with no network hit; an offline unavailable source (e.g. Obadiah 1:1) is recorded in gaps and still produces a schema-valid dossier without crashing; live bible-api fetch through the cache works with passage expansion. Package imports with zero SDKs (openai/anthropic not installed). Did NOT write the pytest suite or final README (FEAT-003).
